title: Prove pointwise Clifford tensor faithfulness and a width-72 passive ceiling
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This proves **pointwise tensor faithfulness for the full n-axis Clifford group at every width f >= 4n+4**, with normalized Gram bounds I/9 and 17I/9. Coefficients, finite words and their support may be chosen separately at each width. For one fixed complete register program over the Gaussian-dyadic group, **four tests at 4n+4 through 4n+7 decide equality at all positive widths**. Four tests are necessary because of central phases. For nine axes this changes the sufficient window from 69..76 to 40..43.

Start with the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32e014bec9206f3987857e6153ec0fd8058f04e3/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/PROOF.md), [exact result](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32e014bec9206f3987857e6153ec0fd8058f04e3/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/RESULT.json), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32e014bec9206f3987857e6153ec0fd8058f04e3/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/SOURCES.json) and [application](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32e014bec9206f3987857e6153ec0fd8058f04e3/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/APPLICATION.md). This is an enabling proof, exact verification tool and scoped quantitative obstruction. **The complete kappa calculation does not improve.** The [base selected record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/certificates/selected-result.json) remains 605457647/200000000000 = 0.003027288235, with its five framework assumptions unchanged.

The same counting argument covers projectively distinct pure stabilizer maps, including rectangular maps and Pauli projections. With N total input/output axes, their normalized tensor Gram bound is 2I/5 through 8I/5 at every f >= 2N+6. Native scalar factors must be raised to f. This extension is a residual frontend, not a complete nonunitary register compiler.

The actual application sharpens Chris R's retained passive saved-query ceiling. Under exactly its fixed ambient-17, nine-cut/three-response contract, the missing endpoint fails at **every f >= 72**, with worst-case operator error at least **1/3** in each affected coefficient. At f >= 84 its normalized squared error is at least 125/126. The [application receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32e014bec9206f3987857e6153ec0fd8058f04e3/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/APPLICATION-RESULT.json) binds the new bounds to the unchanged source replay. Free owned CLEAR/reset remains granted; no cleanup-cost lower bound is used. Active feedback, new paid calls, native prefixes, changed words and noncolumnwise maps remain outside this contract.

## Task and overlap

Base: canonical main `32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04`, priority revision 7. Scope is changed from `formal-interface-lemma` to this written algebraic theorem and its exact application; no proof-assistant formalization is claimed. [TASK.json](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32e014bec9206f3987857e6153ec0fd8058f04e3/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/TASK.json) preserves the original card. The [canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5236#discussioncomment-19169126) reserves no active caller construction.

The closest predecessor, [PR #5376](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5376), supplies the eight-width fixed-program theorem and the consumed native parser, complete endpoint expansion and quadratic-sum kernel. This contribution adds a pointwise threshold, a positive stability bound on the four selected widths, and the nonunitary stabilizer extension. The prior sharp one-axis window 5..8 and the smaller-class monomial cutoff in [PR #5369](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5369) remain stronger in their domains.

The consumed packages are pinned as retained at the base above. Their published source heads are `848cdce9003262c4b6e02ec4558f302e4fae56ad` for PR #5376 and `db3f8456a3efb425e337337d85dcc43b797888cd` for [PR #4978](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4978). The latter retains the actual native source [PR #4948](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4948) at `86e474038e05f99a76d41f71d81946ad2327e4a4`. Its [uniform-alphabet addendum](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/research/passive-saved-query-ceiling/evidence/frozen/pr4948-saved-query-macro-gate/UNIFORM-ALPHABET-ADDENDUM.md) and [owned-reset clarification](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/research/passive-saved-query-ceiling/evidence/frozen/pr4948-saved-query-macro-gate/OWNED-RESET-CLARIFICATION.md) are mandatory pinned inputs.

Related [PR #5446](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5446) permits nonuniform paid histories, but its full target alphabet has not been proved Clifford here. Its claims are not upgraded. The 2026-10-25 06:39..06:40 UTC refresh covered 383 open PRs and 4,804 Discussion records with complete remote pagination; canonical main was unchanged. A separate Git-object search covered tracked research READMEs, proofs and research documents. Sparse arbitrary sources, historical diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.13 on macOS; standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/audit_mutations.py
```

The registered normal and optimized isolated checks each print:

```text
PASS_POINTWISE_CLIFFORD_AND_STABILIZER_NO_NEW_KAPPA
PASS_PASSIVE_CEILING_FROM_WIDTH_72_NO_NEW_KAPPA
```

The runner ends with `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness outcome=completed`. Complete literal stabilizer censuses reach 36,720 states. Separately implemented literal-Choi and signed-Pauli enumerations agree on all 24 and 11,520 one- and two-axis projective Cliffords. The verifier checks rational infinite tails, 448 finite bounds, exact shifted Gram positivity, 8,893 literal map entries, 3,837 pair inner products and 1,024 signed native C columns. It tests the four phase residues, complete native examples, projection scalars and a literal dirty-return counterexample.

The [mutation audit](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32e014bec9206f3987857e6153ec0fd8058f04e3/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/MUTATIONS.json) rejects four deliberate defects in both modes: the first overlap count, native tensor phase, projection tensor scale and signed-Pauli count. It prints `PASS_EIGHT_POINTWISE_MUTATION_REJECTIONS`. Twelve malformed/out-of-scope controls also pass.

Committed-byte checks and the official 79-file export pass at `32e014bec9206f3987857e6153ec0fd8058f04e3`. All four direct replays pass from a fresh read-only export with Git absent from PATH. All 80 regular files, including its manifest, keep identical bytes and inventory. Export SHA-256: `50f453eee5a501707e713ff08217b420157b3cde2d7a9dcc9122c10a610e0405`.

The application replays the retained author and independent audits of all 39 observations, 104 affected inputs and 5,408 late words, and matches the complete frozen output. The all-dimension and all-width statements remain written proofs. These are author checks with separate computational paths, not independent human review or proof-kernel verification. No new provider campaign, selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, physical emission, full pricing or outer admission ran. The full-history ancestry preflight is omitted in this shallow checkout; exact committed objects and source bytes are checked.

## Credit

New proof, tools and application by Ali Romman (@aliromman), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. The earlier PR #5376 methods and source kernels remain predecessor work. Chris R (@Clear1nsight) supplies the passive ceiling and its independent grade/trace audit. Dugongue supplies its actual native source. Their [retained attribution](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/research/passive-saved-query-ceiling/NOTICE.md) and the [native lineage notice](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/research/clifford-tensor-gram/vendor/NATIVE-LINEAGE-NOTICE) preserve the controller, scalar and native predecessors. No predecessor file is edited.

The stabilizer normal form follows [Dehaene and De Moor](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0304125). The residual-form, Pauli-character, Gram and Fourier tools are classical. Krzysztof Wojt and Nick Petalas supply related repository residual-form work, as credited in the [retained completion proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/research/singular-rank-two-pauli/PROOF.md). No global literature-priority claim is made.

## Open next questions

Find the sharp pointwise threshold or bind one actual changed caller to this theorem, with its correct paid history and complete invoice. A source-bound nonunitary caller is also open. The [next questions](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32e014bec9206f3987857e6153ec0fd8058f04e3/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/README.md#open-next-questions) state the first steps and blockers. None is reserved by this contribution.
